featured_reviews.name: Neiladri Chakravarty
featured_reviews.review_text:
This might be the best seated roadside stall ever. Get the keema pav, kulcha, kaleji fry, whatever honesty, it's all good. It's run in front of a home and the service is incredibly fast. You order, sit down and within 5 minutes, your whole steaming dinner is in front of you. Sometimes the uncle forgets one dish because of the insane number of orders pouring in, but you remind him and he serves it to you with a warm smile.

It's got a makeshift seating arrangement on the side of the road, and an elevated surface to eat as well. The eating experience might not be to everyone's liking due to the sheer openness of the place, but I liked the homely communal vibe!

Do not forget to eat at Reva's if you're in Dadar. Just remember that they don't operate every day: select few nights, from 8 to 10.30 ish (?).

featured_reviews.name: Sachin Sonawane
featured_reviews.review_text:
I recently tried the much-hyped batata vada at Shree Krishna Batata Wada in Dadar, and honestly, I was left disappointed. The taste was quite ordinary — nothing extraordinary or unique about it. I had high expectations given the name and long-standing reputation, but the flavor didn’t stand out at all. To top it off, the pricing was shockingly high — ₹27 for just one single vada (not even a plate!). For a simple street snack that’s supposed to be pocket-friendly and satisfying, this felt like a complete rip-off.

There was no chutney or accompaniment that enhanced the taste, and the vada itself lacked spice and crunch. It felt like they were cashing in purely on the legacy or nostalgia rather than actual quality or taste. In a city like Mumbai, where you get amazing batata vadas at countless local joints, this place didn’t meet expectations at all.

If you're a true batata vada lover, I’d suggest exploring other options around Dadar or even in nearby areas — there are definitely better places in terms of both taste and value for money. My honest opinion — a BIG NO to this place. Not worth the hype or the price.

featured_reviews.name: Suryaprakash Barnwal
featured_reviews.review_text:
Ashok Vada Pav near Kirti College, Dadar definitely attracts a huge crowd. We reached around 2:15 PM and still had to wait close to 40 minutes in the queue before getting served, which itself shows how popular the place is.

The location is definitely a plus point since it’s close to Dadar Beach. The highlight for me was the crispy chura, which added a unique crunch and gave the vada pav a different texture compared to regular stalls.

However, the overall experience felt a bit overrated for the wait and pricing. The service was slow, there was no extra chutney or extra chura provided, and the vada pavs were simply wrapped in paper and handed over. Since everything is pre-made, there’s almost no scope for customization in terms of chutney or spice level like you usually get at local vendors. Personally, I also found the taste slightly too sweet.

The pricing is ₹35 for a single vada pav and ₹140 for four pieces, which feels almost double compared to many other local vendors offering similar or even better taste.

Overall, it’s worth trying once for the hype and experience, but personally I don’t think the taste and service justify waiting more than 40 minutes when there are plenty of local places serving equally good vada pav with faster service, better customization, and more value for money.

featured_reviews.review_text:
After taking blessings at Shree Siddhivinayak Temple, a visit to Ashok Vada Pav is almost a ritual for food lovers. The vada pav here is served hot and fresh, with a perfectly crispy vada, soft pav, and flavorful chutneys that make every bite memorable.
One of the best experiences is to take a parcel and head towards Dadar Chowpatty. Sitting by the sea, enjoying the view and cool breeze while eating this iconic vada pav creates a combination that's hard to beat. The joy of having Ashok Vada Pav with the sea view is something truly special.
The long queue outside the stall speaks for itself. Just looking at the crowd, you can tell how popular this place is. It's not famous without reason—the taste, consistency, and quality have made it a favorite among Mumbaikars and tourists alike for years.

• Texture: The combination of the vada with the crispy "chura" is definitely interesting and adds a nice crunch.

The Not-So-Good:
• The Wait: Be prepared to stand in line. It took me between 20-30 minutes just to get served.

featured_reviews.review_text: Hands down one of the tastiest vada pav you’ll find in Mumbai. The vada is perfectly crispy outside, soft inside, and packed with flavour. The chutneys add the perfect spicy kick that makes every bite addictive. It’s always super crowded with a long queue, but it’s absolutely worth the wait. featured_reviews.name: Naresh Shirodkar
featured_reviews.review_text:
In a city that runs on speed, spice, and soul, some places don’t just serve food, they become emotion. Ashok Vada Pav near Kirti College is exactly that kind of institution, where generations have stood shoulder to shoulder, waiting for that one perfect bite.
What makes their vada pav truly iconic is the balance. The batata vada is crisp on the outside, soft and flavourful inside, with just the right hint of garlic and spice. The pav is always fresh, lightly toasted, and acts as the perfect carrier without overpowering the star.
But the real magic lies in their chutney game. That signature dry garlic chutney hits instantly with a bold, smoky spice, while the fried green chillies on the side elevate the entire experience. It’s not just heat, it’s character, the kind that lingers and keeps you coming back.
And then comes the cult favourite, the chura pav. Buttery, spicy, slightly messy, and absolutely addictive. The crushed vada mixed with chutneys and masala, soaked into the pav, creates a texture and flavour bomb that feels indulgent in the most Mumbai way possible. Crisp edges, soft centres, and that unmistakable street-style richness.
Being a true Dadarkar, I’ve grown up eating this vada pav, and what’s incredible is how the taste has remained exactly the same over the years, still the best vada pav, hands down.
There’s a legacy here that you can actually taste. Started decades ago and now run by the next generation, Ashok Vada Pav has become a landmark in Dadar’s food scene. It has seen college crowds, office rush, late-night hunger, and everything in between, yet the consistency remains untouched. No unnecessary reinvention, just doing the basics exceptionally well, every single time. The vibe is classic Mumbai, fast-moving queues, minimal waiting despite the crowd, and an energy that feels alive. You don’t come here for luxury, you come here for authenticity.
Ashok Vada Pav isn’t just food, it’s a ritual, a memory, and for many, a weekly craving that never fades.
Simple, iconic, and absolutely unbeatable. 🌶️🔥

Dadar Surti Farsan Mart is one of those places that every foodie in Mumbai has strong opinions about, and after trying them, I can finally see why. I stopped by recently to grab a quick snack, and here is my honest take on the experience.

The Food (The Star of the Show):
Let's get straight to the point—their samosa is exceptional. The outer shell is perfectly crisp and flaky, not too thick, and shatters beautifully when you bite into it. The filling inside is well-spiced and flavorful without being too greasy. But what truly elevates the entire experience is their chutney. It is an absolute game-changer. It strikes that perfect balance between sweet, tangy, and spicy, complementing the samosa so well that you will find yourself asking for extra portions. If you are a samosa connoisseur, this is a must-try.

The Vibe & Service:
Being a farsan mart, it operates with that classic "counter-service" efficiency. It can get quite crowded, especially during evening snack time, so be prepared to wait a few minutes to place your order. The staff is efficient, though they are clearly accustomed to the rush.

The Price Factor:
Now, onto the one point that keeps this from being a perfect 5-star review for me: the pricing. There is no denying that the quality is top-tier, but the cost is undeniably on the higher side compared to your average local snack joint. You are paying a premium for the brand name and the location. While the taste justifies the splurge occasionally, it is the kind of place you go to when you want a "treat yourself" snack rather than an everyday cheap eat.

Verdict:
If you love samosas and want to taste one of the best versions available in Mumbai, you have to visit Dadar Surti Farsan Mart. Just go in knowing that your wallet will feel a slightly lighter for the experience

Their Batata Vada, Dhokla, Samosa, Bhajiya, and many other varieties of farsan are a must-try! If you're in the mood for something more, don't miss their Samosa and Khandvi, both of which are deliciously flavorful. The chutney they serve alongside adds a perfect tangy kick to the snacks.

featured_reviews.name: Rajat Bajaj
featured_reviews.review_text:
On a rainy Sunday, I visited Dadar Surti Farsan, a well-known spot for traditional Gujarati snacks, and the experience was absolutely delightful. The drizzle outside made it the perfect day to indulge in some hot and savory farsan, and this place did not disappoint. The shop has a simple, no-fuss vibe, but what truly stands out is the freshness and authenticity of the food served.

I began with their **soft and spongy dhokla**, which was perfectly steamed, light on the stomach, and mildly tangy with just the right hint of sweetness. Topped with mustard seeds and curry leaves, it had that authentic Gujarati touch. Next, I tried the makai roll, which was both unique and flavorful. The subtle sweetness of corn paired with the spices made it a wholesome snack and something I’d definitely go back for.

The highlight for me, however, was the pyaz kachori. Crispy on the outside and generously stuffed with a spicy onion mixture inside, it was comfort food at its best—especially when enjoyed hot on a rainy day. Each bite was bursting with flavor and paired perfectly with the chutneys served alongside.

One of the best parts about Dadar Surti Farsan is its **reasonable pricing**. Despite the quality and freshness of the items, the rates are pocket-friendly, making it a great place for both quick bites and takeaway parcels. The staff was quick and efficient, ensuring customers didn’t have to wait long even though the place was quite busy.

Overall, my visit to Dadar Surti Farsan was an enjoyable mix of great taste, tradition, and value for money. For anyone who enjoys authentic Gujarati snacks, this place is a must-try and the experience becomes even more special when savored on a rainy day.

featured_reviews.name: Sumit K
featured_reviews.review_text:
Aswad Restaurant is an excellent place for anyone looking to enjoy authentic Maharashtrian vegetarian food in a clean, comfortable, and welcoming environment in dadar mumbai. The restaurant maintains very high standards of hygiene, which adds greatly to the overall dining experience.

The food is not only delicious but also very affordable, making it a great option for regular meals as well as for first-time visitors wanting to explore traditional Maharashtrian cuisine. Their **Maharashtrian thali** is highly recommended, offering a wholesome and satisfying combination of flavors. Special dishes like **Bhakri–Pithla** and **Thalipeeth** are prepared perfectly and taste truly homely.

One of the highlights of Aswad is their **Modak**, which is simply the best—fresh, flavorful, and a must-try for dessert lovers. The food is mild, not overly spicy or oily, making it suitable for all age groups and ideal for those who prefer healthy, home-style meals.

The service is polite, prompt, and courteous, adding to the pleasant atmosphere of the restaurant. Its convenient location near **Dadar Metro Station** makes it easily accessible in mumbai.

Overall, Aswad Restaurant is a wonderful choice for hygienic, affordable, and authentic Maharashtrian vegetarian food with a comforting, home-cooked feel. Highly recommended.

Prakash Shakahari Upahar is a familiar old-school spot in Dadar, popular for traditional Maharashtrian breakfast items. My experience was mixed and mostly average.
I tried the Thalipith, which was genuinely good in taste and felt fresh—easily the best item I had. The misal was average and surprisingly mild, lacking the expected spice punch. The tea was honestly quite bad, with poor taste and no real depth.
One thoughtful and uncommon decision is that they don’t serve pav at all. While many may not like this, I actually appreciated the intent—it feels health-conscious and shows they’re thinking beyond pure business.
Prices are normal and reasonable. Seating, however, is very limited, and during breakfast hours you should expect a 30–40 minute waiting time, which can test your patience.
⚠️ Important Note:
They do not accept UPI online payments, or cards. Cash payment only, so come prepared.
Overall:
A simple, traditional place with one or two good items, long waiting times, and very old-school operations. Worth visiting for Thalipith if you’re nearby, but don’t go in expecting bold flavors or modern convenience.

featured_reviews.name: Vinit Vinayak
featured_reviews.review_text:
I recently visited Muthuswamy Cafe, and it was an amazing experience for anyone who loves authentic South Indian food.

The place has a simple yet comforting vibe, and the aroma itself sets the mood as soon as you walk in. The food is absolutely top-notch—fresh, flavorful, and perfectly balanced. From crispy dosas to soft idlis and rich sambhar, everything tasted authentic and satisfying.

The service was quick and efficient, and the staff was polite and attentive throughout. It’s one of those places where you go for the food and end up loving the whole experience.

If you’re in Dadar and craving real South Indian flavors, this spot is definitely worth visiting!

featured_reviews.name: Himanshi Patel
featured_reviews.review_text: Café Muthuswami in Dadar is a cozy spot that brings authentic South Indian flavors to life. Known for its crispy dosas, soft idlis, and rich, aromatic filter coffee, every bite feels comforting and nostalgic. The ambiance is simple yet inviting, perfect for casual catch-ups or a relaxed solo meal. Service is quick, and the food quality is consistently impressive. Whether you’re craving a hearty breakfast or a light evening snack, this café delivers on both taste and experience. A must-visit for anyone who loves traditional South Indian food in Mumbai with a homely touch and great value.

featured_reviews.name: Pooja Fulsundar
featured_reviews.review_text:
Mutuswami Cafe is located just outside Dadar East railway station, so it’s very easy to find and perfect for a quick stop after travel. They have both indoor and outdoor seating, which is nice if you want to sit comfortably or just grab something quickly.
We tried the strawberry milkshake & mango milkshake both were thick, chilled, and refreshing. The paper masala dosa was big, crispy, and came with good chutney and sambar. Kanchipuram idli was soft and flavourful, a little different from regular idli and worth trying.
Cheese tava rice was spicy, cheesy, and filling good if you’re very hungry. We ended with pineapple sheera, which was warm, slightly sweet, and had a nice fruity taste.
Overall, it’s a good place for South Indian food and quick snacks near the station.

featured_reviews.name: VISHAL UPADHYAY
featured_reviews.review_text: We ordered cheese pav bhaji, and masala dosa and both were extremely delicious. We loved both the items. Cost wise it appeared a little costly given the ambience, and quality of service. It was situated near Dadar railway station and is fine for some snacking.

featured_reviews.name: Gayatri
featured_reviews.review_text:
If you’re in Dadar and craving authentic South Indian flavors any time of the day, Muttuswami Cafe is the place to be!
This is the only café in the area open 24/7, making it a perfect spot for early breakfasts, late-night cravings, or casual meetups at any hour.
The food quality is outstanding, with every dish served fresh, flavorful, and satisfying:
Cheese Pav Bhaji – perfectly buttery with a generous layer of melted cheese that elevates the classic taste.
Podi Idli – soft, bite-sized idlis coated beautifully in spicy podi masala and ghee.
Muttuswami Special Benne Dosa – rich, crispy, and soaked in butter with a delicious traditional touch.
Spring Dosa – a unique fusion twist, crispy outside with a flavorful stuffed filling inside.
Fruit Custard Dessert – creamy, refreshing, and loaded with fresh fruits for the perfect sweet ending.
Their fresh juices are equally impressive — especially the pomegranate juice and the orange-mosambi mix, both refreshing and naturally sweet.
What truly makes the experience special is the warm and polite staff. The service is quick, attentive, and always delivered with a smile. The beautiful interiors create a clean, cozy, and welcoming atmosphere, making you want to sit back and enjoy your meal.

Food was amazing tasty. A little higher price.. people may feel for this .. however if you compare to food outlets in the mall .. it's the same. Combos one can have .. quantity fulfills  the hunger for one person. Overall nice experience. Recommended if around Dadar railway station.

They have indoor and outdoor seating. Post 8 pm it's a busy schedule for the restaurant so go a bit early to get the best available table of the house.

Our food recommendations.

Podi Idli:
You have to visit this place to experience this extraordinary delicacy of the house .

Benne Masala Dosa:
This one won't disappoint you if you are fond of benne then definitely give this a try.

Pav Bhaji:

The Mango Milkshake was rich and thick  . Even their cold coffee has a supreme vibe.
